question: Which of the following key combinations can be used in the Windows version of the MS- Word to insert current time?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alt + Shift + t**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alt + Shift + T: **This combination doesn't insert the **current time in Microsoft Word**. Instead, it's used in Adobe programs for different functionalities, such as opening new layer options in Adobe Photoshop.
 
• **Alt + T: **In a lot of programs, this opens a "Tools" menu if one is available. However, in Microsoft Word, this command doesn't have a default action assigned.
 
• **Alt + Ctrl + T: **This combination is not a default shortcut in Microsoft Word. It might be designated for a specific function in some other software packages, but in general, and in Microsoft Word specifically, it doesn't perform a specific operation by default.
 
• **Shift + T**: If you press this while writing, it will simply type the capital letter 'T'. It doesn't perform any special operation in Microsoft Word.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alt + N**, then** D**: This is a **two-step shortcut**. First, you press Alt + N to open the insert tab in the MS Word menu bar. Then, press 'D' for the Date and Time dialog box, where you can choose a format and insert the current time.
 
• **Alt + Shift + D**: This inserts the current date in MS Word.
